cards.title: The Hidden Costs of Forgetting: A Study of Trajectory Deletion in Software Engineering Agents
cards.what: An empirical study of 42 trajectory-reduction configurations across 9,400 runs with two agents on SWE-bench Verified. Deleting large amounts of old-turn content, even all reasoning text, can preserve effectiveness if delayed. Agents re-fetch deleted content. Under caching-aware pricing, no configuration lowered costs.
cards.why_you: It is evidence on context management for coding agents, your top interest. It suggests that trimming context in your own harness may not save money once prompt caching is counted, which is relevant to long scheduled runs and subagent design.

cards.next_step: Read the case study on how prescribed steps skipped decisive evidence, then ask which of your agents have fixed stages that a looser prompt could replace.
cards.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
cards.what: A comparison on 90 validated microservice failure cases. Three simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls beat five published hand-crafted root cause analysis agents (PR at 1 of 65 to 77 percent versus 16 to 53 percent). More reasoning effort added few points but multiplied time up to seven times.
cards.why_you: It is harness-design evidence: open-ended investigation beat fixed stages and role agents. That bears on how prescriptive your reader, reviewer and plan-gate agents should be. The domain is microservice diagnosis, not coding, so the fit is partial.

title: ☕ Tech Digest — Tue 27 Oct 2026

top.headline: Claude Code 2.1.311 fixes a pile of subagent, hook and compaction bugs
top.summary: The release fixes long startup freezes when a CLAUDE.md holds a very long list item, subagents unable to use MCP tools from servers that finish connecting late, and stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction. SubagentStop hooks no longer run about twice a minute per running subagent. Standard-context sessions that run over 200K tokens now compact and continue instead of stopping with a usage-credits error.
top.title: Claude Code 2.1.311
top.why: Subagents, hooks, compaction and CLAUDE.md behaviour are the top of your list, and this release touches all four.

top.headline: Study asks why agents survive deleting old trajectory turns, and what it costs
top.summary: Software engineering agents resend their whole trajectory to the model every turn, which motivates trimming it. Earlier work showed randomly deleting 75% of tokens in old turns may preserve agent effectiveness. This paper asks why, how agents compensate for the missing content, and what the hidden costs are.
top.title: The Hidden Costs of Forgetting: A Study of Trajectory Deletion in Software Engineering Agents
top.why: Context-management techniques with evidence are on your want list, and this one examines what trimming costs an agent.

top.headline: Simple LLM harnesses outdiagnose hand-crafted root cause analysis agents
top.summary: Many LLM agents for root cause analysis of microservice failures use hand-crafted investigation: standard operating procedures, fixed stages and role agents. Each is evaluated on its own data against few baselines, so it is unknown whether the design beats giving a model free rein. The paper's title reports that simple harnesses win.
top.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
top.why: A result on harness design with a comparison against baselines, which is the kind of evidence you asked for on what works in agent setups.
